title: What to do with a duplicate card
target: What to do with the second, third and fourth copy of a card in TCG Card Shop Simulator: keeping one in the album, selling or donating the rest, binning what will not move, and when grading is worth the wait.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A card you already own a copy of
The shop open, with the album or the counter within reach
An idea of what the card sells for

steps.do: Put the first copy in the album before deciding anything about the rest.
steps.because: cards are kept in an album whose binder pages track the index of the card they hold, and looking through the album is a mode you enter and leave (DelayHideCardAlbum, DelaySetBinderPageCardIndex, DelayExitViewCardAlbumMode)

steps.do: Price the spare from the game's own information rather than from memory.
steps.because: a card carries a price tag of its own and the price can be checked on a screen of its own (InteractableCardPriceTag, CheckPriceScreen)

steps.do: Sell the ordinary duplicates on a shelf rather than hoarding them in a box.
steps.because: what is on a shelf and what is in a box are tracked separately, so a spare is either display stock or storage (ShelfManager, InteractablePackagingBox_Card)

steps.do: Use the donation box for the spares that are not worth pricing.
steps.because: there is a bulk donation box for cards, with a panel of its own (BulkDonationBoxCardPanelUI)

steps.do: Bin what will not move instead of storing it forever.
steps.because: cards are also removed in the shop, with kinds of removal, a confirmation screen and a list of bins of its own (ECardRemoveType, ConfirmTrashCardScreen, m_TrashBinList)

steps.do: Check what grading would cost before you send anything.
steps.because: a grading service has a name, a number of days and a cost per card, and the submit screen breaks the total into per-card cost and a delivery fee (GradeCardServiceData, m_ServiceName, m_ServiceDays, m_CostPerCard, GradedCardSubmitSelectScreen)

steps.do: Only send cards you can afford to wait for.
steps.because: a submission holds the cards, the service level and the time that has passed, and can be checked while it is away (GradeCardSubmitSet, m_CardDataList, m_ServiceLevel, m_DayPassed, GradedCardSetCheckStatusScreen)

steps.do: Expect graded cards back through a sequence of their own.
steps.because: graded cards come back through an opening sequence rather than straight onto the shelf (GradedCardOpeningSequence, m_CardRevealFromBoxAnim)

steps.do: Keep the spares a deck needs before you sell the rest.
steps.because: the play table's items include the playmat, the deck box and the cards, so a spare can have a use that is not selling (TableGameItemSet, m_DeckBoxMesh, m_PlayMatMesh)

commonMistakes: Filing the spare in the album and the original in a box, the wrong way round.
Sending a cheap card to grading because the service was already open.
Binning cards the bulk donation box would have taken.
Selling the copies a deck needs because they happened to be the ones in hand.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
